name: Tanning mitt
lead: A tanning mitt is a thin glove, often velvet-like or latex-lined, used to apply self-tanner evenly and keep the hands from being stained.
It is the usual accessory for sunless tanning, especially for avoiding orange palms.

paras: The mitt spreads the product in a thin even layer through a smoothing motion, and barrier lining prevents DHA from staining the hands. It has no tanning action of its own, so there is no mitt-specific research; its role follows from how DHA behaves on skin.

Mitts have no meaningful safety risk, though residue builds up and the mitt should be washed or replaced to avoid streaks. A mitt cannot fix poor prep, and skipping exfoliation still leads to patchy color. The claim that it avoids orange palms is plausible and widely reported, though not tested in trials.

studies.title: Properties and safety of topical dihydroxyacetone in sunless tanning products: A review
